method: Candidates from merged PRs / closed issues in the fixed window (protocol §5b), adjudicated with Q1 (latent at T0) / Q2 (maintainers acted, explicit reason) / Q3 (discoverable from T0 repository evidence by code review). All T0 facts verified against the snapshot workspace. Buckets: included (main Recall) / ambiguous (not in Recall) / excluded (exploratory) / reject (new features, external changes, not-latent).

candidates.change: PR #5928: 'all teardown callbacks are called despite errors' — collect errors from all teardown callbacks instead of stopping at the first failing one
candidates.possible_root: do_teardown_request runs callbacks in a loop without per-handler error isolation; one raising callback terminates the chain and skips remaining cleanup
candidates.t0_evidence: src/flask/app.py do_teardown_request: 'for func in reversed(self.teardown_request_funcs[name]): self.ensure_sync(func)(exc)' — no try/except per handler; docs (api.rst teardown section) stated callbacks 'must not fail'
candidates.future_evidence: #5870 describes skipped critical cleanup when a non-critical teardown raises; #5928 (merged in window) changed semantics so all callbacks run and errors are collected (ExceptionGroup on 3.11+)
candidates.why_researcher_could_detect: Direct code review of do_teardown_request: a chain that aborts on the first exception is visible; the doc contract 'must not fail' contradicts standard robustness expectations
candidates.category: later-exposed existing bug root cause / architecture debt

candidates.change: PR #5917: 'fix provide_automatic_options override' — OPTIONS route now added correctly whenever provide_automatic_options is set; previously it could only be disabled, not enabled
candidates.possible_root: add_url_rule only adds OPTIONS to required_methods inside the default (None) branch; an explicit True leaves OPTIONS out of the rule's methods so the dispatch-time auto-OPTIONS check never fires
candidates.t0_evidence: src/flask/sansio/app.py add_url_rule: 'if provide_automatic_options is None:' fallback chain — required_methods.add('OPTIONS') only when the value defaults from config; src/flask/app.py dispatch_request (line ~983): 'getattr(rule, "provide_automatic_options", False) and req.method == "OPTIONS"'
candidates.future_evidence: #5916 documents the weirdness and the enable path failure; #5917 (merged in window, fixes #5916) 'Previously, it was only added if the argument was not passed and was not set as an attribute; it could only be disabled, not enabled'
candidates.why_researcher_could_detect: Code review of add_url_rule vs dispatch_request: the explicit-True path never adds OPTIONS to the rule methods, making the automatic response unreachable; inconsistent with the parameter's documented meaning

candidates.change: should_ignore_error deprecated and removed: dead-weight method called once per request that always returns False, undocumented except API list, untested, and whose semantics (hide error from teardown) conflict with the merged app/request context model
candidates.possible_root: legacy method kept from pre-#5812 code; after the context merge its intended behavior no longer exists; extra per-request call with constant result
candidates.t0_evidence: src/flask/sansio/app.py:925 should_ignore_error: docstring 'if True the teardown handlers will not be passed the error' + body 'return False'; called at src/flask/app.py:1579 in wsgi_app finally on every request; no tests reference it
candidates.future_evidence: #5816 (pre-T0, still open at T0): 'It results in an extra function call every single request, only to always return false'; #5899 merged in window deprecating/removing it
candidates.why_researcher_could_detect: Code review: a method that always returns False yet is invoked per request is dead weight; its docstring describes behavior (error hiding) that contradicts the current error flow

candidates.change: Tutorial app aborts if the instance folder cannot be created instead of silently ignoring the error
candidates.possible_root: canonical tutorial example swallows OSError when creating the instance folder; a PermissionError therefore goes unnoticed and the app runs against a nonexistent instance dir
candidates.t0_evidence: examples/tutorial/flaskr/__init__.py: 'try: os.makedirs(app.instance_path) except OSError: pass' — silent error swallowing in the tutorial's factory function
candidates.future_evidence: #5903 (merged in window): 'According to the comment, the instance folder should exist in any case. But a PermissionError was ignored silently.' — changed to abort; docs/tutorial/factory.rst updated
candidates.why_researcher_could_detect: Code review of the tutorial example: bare except OSError: pass hides a failure that contradicts the comment 'ensure the instance folder exists'

candidates.change: docs/patterns/javascript.rst 'Receiving JSON in Views' corrected: wrong/missing Content-Type raises 415, not 400; 400 only for invalid JSON body
candidates.possible_root: documentation drift: the JavaScript-patterns page claimed 400 for both invalid JSON and wrong Content-Type, contradicting the API reference and actual behavior
candidates.t0_evidence: docs/patterns/javascript.rst at T0: 'If the body is not valid JSON, or the Content-Type header is not set to application/json, a 400 Bad Request error will be raised'; API reference (flask.Request.json) and werkzeug behavior raise 415 UnsupportedMediaType for missing/wrong Content-Type
candidates.future_evidence: #5825 (pre-T0, still open at T0) quoting the contradiction; #5827 merged in window: 'Clarifies the distinction between 415 and 400... aligning the JavaScript patterns documentation with the API reference' (+5/-3 in docs/patterns/javascript.rst)
candidates.why_researcher_could_detect: Internal documentation inconsistency: two official docs pages disagree about the same behavior; code path (on_json_loading_failed → 415) confirms which one is wrong

candidates.change: No in-window code fix confirmed; #5812 (merged pre-T0, 2025-09-19) was claimed to fix it but a 2025-09-29 test against 3.2.0.dev0 still reproduced it
candidates.possible_root: 3.1.2 stream_with_context refactor (#5799) invokes teardown_request too early (before response generation) and twice for streamed responses
candidates.t0_evidence: stream_with_context / teardown lifecycle in app.py at T0; users pinned flask <3.1.2; maintainer confirmed the issue and deferred the fix to 3.2
candidates.future_evidence: conflicting: maintainer said 'fixed as a side effect of #5812' but #5812 merged pre-T0 and the issue stayed open with reproduction against 3.2.0.dev0 in-window; no fix PR in the window; issue closed 2026-01-25 without a visible resolution
candidates.why_researcher_could_detect: Hard: requires reasoning about streaming response lifetime; the teardown-timing defect is not obvious from static reading of app.py alone
candidates.category: evidence conflict — not confirmable in window
candidates.exclusion_reason: Q2 (acted on with explicit reason) fails within the window; fix evidence contradictory. Per instruction: do not force ambiguous evidence into main Recall. Saved for exploratory analysis.

candidates.possible_root: 302 for POST redirects causes browsers to re-submit the request; 303 is the spec-preferred code
candidates.t0_evidence: src/flask/helpers.py redirect(location, code=302) default at T0
candidates.future_evidence: #5898 merged in window with explicit rationale; #5895 documents the issue
candidates.why_researcher_could_detect: Partially: reading the default + HTTP knowledge could flag it, but it reads as a deliberate behavior default rather than a defect
candidates.category: behavior preference / spec-compliance decision — protocol §4 excludes 'maintainer changed preference'
candidates.exclusion_reason: Closer to a preference change than a latent defect; not in main Recall.
